tasks.title: Master key via an external key service (OpenBao Transit) - the worker never holds it

scenarios: The master key never resides in the worker and seal/unseal calls the external key service

tasks.status_evidence: Verified 2026-08-23 against the tree: core/seal/transit.go wraps the DEK through OpenBao Transit (/v1/transit/encrypt|decrypt/<key>), so the master-key operation runs INSIDE the substrate and the key never exists in this process; core/seal/fromenv.go selects Transit FIRST when configured. Oracles green this run: TestSealerTransitRoundTrip (real endpoint paths asserted, and a DEK the substrate refuses fails closed to ErrOpenFailed), TestNewTransitWrapperFailClosed (every missing-config direction), and TestTransitWinsOverALocalMasterKeyWhenBothAreConfigured — whose header documents the executed killing mutation (check the local key first ⇒ RED, the weaker posture wins). The pending status was stale bookkeeping, not missing work.

tasks.title: Split the read-only triage plane from the actuation-credential plane (disjoint OpenBao roles)

scenarios: The read-only triage plane cannot resolve an actuation credential

tasks.status_evidence: TG-153, 2026-08-04. SUBSTRATE (done by hand, verified live): OpenBao policies tg-triage-ro (read secret/data/tg/*, DENY tg/actuator + tg/proxmox) and tg-actuate-ro (read ONLY tg/actuator + tg/proxmox), bound to AppRoles tg-triage / tg-actuate. Measured: triage token -> tg/actuator 403, hostdiag 200; actuate token -> tg/actuator 200, hostdiag 403. PROCESS: TG_CREDENTIAL_PLANE = triage|actuation|both (default both = the pre-TG-153 posture, byte-identical, so no existing deployment changes on upgrade). core/credential/plane_split.go gains ProcessPlane + PlaneSet.ValidateFor, which refuses a triage process holding ANY actuation reference and vice versa; cmd/worker/credential_plane.go withholds off-plane configuration at ACQUISITION so the credential is never resolved and never resident; temporal/runner routes the estate-mutating activity onto the tg.actuate queue that only the actuation worker polls; deploy/docker-compose.yml adds the opt-in worker-actuate service (split-planes profile). Oracles with executed killing mutations: TestTriagePlaneCannotReachAnyActuationCredential, TestActuationPlaneCannotReachAnyUntrustedContentSource, TestTriagePlaneRefusesAnyActuationRef, TestActuationActivityIsScheduledOnTheActuationQueue, plus the no-regression pair TestBothPlaneIsByteIdenticalToTheHistoricCheck / TestBothPlaneIsIdenticalToPreSplitBehaviour. NOT closed by this task: T-022-3 (just-in-time SSH identity) is still pending — the actuation worker holds a long-lived key, it just holds it alone. docs/THREAT-MODEL.md §5.1 states the resulting blast-radius bound and its residuals.

tasks.title: cosign image-signing key stored in OpenBao; sign-on-build + verify-before-deploy

scenarios: The image-signing key is resolved from the substrate, not a plaintext CI variable

tasks.status_evidence: SUPERSEDED, not merely unbuilt (verified 2026-08-23 against .gitlab-ci.yml:996-998): the cosign sign+verify supply-chain gate was REMOVED by owner decision (TG-417) because the registry did not durably retain the signatures — they were signed and dropped within hours, so cosign-verify reddened every main pipeline and BLOCKED EVERY DEPLOY. Storing the signing key in OpenBao would restore a chain the project deliberately retired; the provenance need it served is now carried by the SBOM job (.gitlab-ci.yml:350) plus the deployed-SHA witness. Re-opening this task means re-deciding the gate first, which is an owner call, not build work.
